description: A read-only historian sent six Modbus write requests to a line 2 controller. Confirmed and contained. Keywords: hunt, true-positive, ics, modbus, t0836.
title: __RUN_DATE__ | CLIENT-A | Hunt: unauthorised Modbus writes to line 2 controller (T0836) | Closed - True Positive | TLP:AMBER

eventNotes.note: First write request: WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER from the historian. IOC: source.ip 10.50.2.30.
WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS: several registers rewritten in one request. The Zeek log does not show which.
WRITE_SINGLE_COIL: an output or flag was switched. Which coil and its state are not in this data.

globalNotes.note:
TLP:AMBER | CLIENT-A

## Hypothesis
Something other than an authorised writer is changing values on the line 2 controller.

## Scope and data
Zeek on the line 2 OT network sensor, Modbus/TCP (zeek.modbus log). Authorised writers on this zone: ot-eng-ws-01 and ot-hmi-01. All other hosts should only read. Assets by IP (the sensor sees addresses, not names): ot-eng-ws-01 10.50.1.20, ot-hmi-01 10.50.2.10, ot-hist-01 10.50.2.30, plc-line2-01 10.50.3.11, plc-line2-02 10.50.3.12, ot-jump-01 10.50.0.5.

## Queries run
- zeek.modbus.function is one of WRITE_SINGLE_COIL, WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER, WRITE_MULTIPLE_COILS, WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS
- AND source.ip is not one of 10.50.1.20, 10.50.2.10 (authorised writers)

## Findings
Six Modbus write requests to plc-line2-01 (10.50.3.11) from 10.50.2.30, ot-hist-01, the historian, over about seven minutes: WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER three times, WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS once and WRITE_SINGLE_COIL twice. In the baseline the historian sends only READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS. Treated as true positive: a read-only host is writing to a controller. The Zeek Modbus log records the function but not register addresses or values, so what was changed is not in this data. The plant owner must check the controller, or a packet capture, for the affected setpoints, alarm limits and outputs.

## Incident handling (NIST SP 800-61 phases)
- Detect: Hunt, OT protocol write allowlist
- Analyse: Six writes from a read-only host, sequence pinned
- Contain: Historian isolated at the zone firewall after client approval; controller values checked and restored by the plant operator
- Eradicate: Historian rebuilt; how it was accessed is under investigation
- Recover: Writes from outside the allowlist now alert

## NIS2 reporting (example of use, not a compliance claim)
Reportable? Yes, to assess by the client against its thresholds
Clock started at: [UTC time the client became aware]
Early warning 24h: [done] | Notification 72h: [done] | Final report 1 month: [drafted]

## Handover
Closed. Plant owner to confirm which registers and coils changed (packet capture or controller audit) and that they are back to their intended values. Keep the Modbus write allowlist detection.

Keywords: hunt, true-positive, ics, modbus, t0836
Report-ready summary: Six Modbus write requests from the read-only historian reached a line 2 controller; true positive, contained, changed values to be confirmed by the plant owner (TLP:AMBER).

eqlOptions.query:
sequence by source.ip, destination.ip with maxspan=15m
  [network where zeek.modbus.function == "READ_HOLDING_REGISTERS"]
  [network where zeek.modbus.function in ("WRITE_SINGLE_COIL", "WRITE_SINGLE_REGISTER", "WRITE_MULTIPLE_COILS", "WRITE_MULTIPLE_REGISTERS")
    and not cidrMatch(source.ip, "10.50.1.20/32", "10.50.2.10/32")]

description: A vendor account failed four times then logged on to the line 2 HMI over RDP from an IT address, not the jump host. Confirmed and contained. Keywords: hunt, true-positive, ics, remote-access, t0886.
title: __RUN_DATE__ | CLIENT-A | Hunt: remote desktop logons to the HMI from the IT network (T0886) | Closed - True Positive | TLP:AMBER

eventNotes.note: First failed logon for svc-vendor, wrong password for a valid account. IOC: source.ip 10.20.4.77, workstation ITWS-0417.
Successful RDP logon 48 seconds after the first failure. IOC: user svc-vendor.
Second RDP logon about 24 minutes later from the same source.

globalNotes.note:
TLP:AMBER | CLIENT-A

## Hypothesis
Someone is reaching the OT zone over remote desktop without going through the jump host.

## Scope and data
Windows Security events (4624, 4625) from the HMI ot-hmi-01. The only approved remote path into the zone is the jump host ot-jump-01 (10.50.0.5).

## Queries run
- winlog.logon.type is RemoteInteractive (RDP)
- AND event.code is one of 4624, 4625
- AND source.ip is not 10.50.0.5 (the jump host)

## Findings
Six events on ot-hmi-01, all RDP (logon type RemoteInteractive) for the account svc-vendor from 10.20.4.77, workstation ITWS-0417, an address in the IT range and not the jump host. Four failed logons (4625, bad password for a valid account) 12 seconds apart, then a successful logon (4624), then a second successful logon about 24 minutes later. In the baseline, RDP to the HMI comes only from the jump host as ops-jump. Treated as true positive: the account was used from outside the approved path after failed attempts.

## Incident handling (NIST SP 800-61 phases)
- Detect: Hunt, remote access hypothesis
- Analyse: Failures then success from a non-approved source, second logon later
- Contain: Account disabled, HMI session ended, RDP to OT hosts restricted to the jump host at the firewall
- Eradicate: Vendor credentials reset; how the account was exposed is under investigation
- Recover: Vendor access re-enabled through the jump host with MFA

## NIS2 reporting (example of use, not a compliance claim)
Reportable? Yes, to assess by the client against its thresholds

Early warning 24h: [done] | Notification 72h: [done] | Final report 1 month: [drafted]

## Handover
Closed. Client to confirm whether the vendor was on site or remote. Keep the detection for RDP from sources other than the jump host.

description: Open at end of shift: an unknown device probed 24 controller addresses on Modbus, S7 and EtherNet/IP ports. Keywords: hunt, handover, ics, discovery, t0846.
title: __RUN_DATE__ | CLIENT-C | Hunt: unknown device scanning OT controllers (T0846) | Open - Handover | TLP:AMBER

eventNotes.note: Probe that completed: 10.50.3.20 port 44818 (EtherNet/IP). No asset on record at this address.

globalNotes.note:
TLP:AMBER | CLIENT-C

## Hypothesis
A device that is not part of the line 2 asset list is mapping the controllers.

## Scope and data
Zeek connection log (zeek.connection) from the line 2 OT network sensor. Allowed to open controller ports: ot-eng-ws-01, ot-hmi-01 and ot-hist-01. Assets by IP (the sensor sees addresses, not names): ot-eng-ws-01 10.50.1.20, ot-hmi-01 10.50.2.10, ot-hist-01 10.50.2.30, plc-line2-01 10.50.3.11, plc-line2-02 10.50.3.12, ot-jump-01 10.50.0.5.

## Queries run
- destination.port is one of 502, 102, 44818 (Modbus, S7, EtherNet/IP)
- AND source.ip is not one of 10.50.1.20, 10.50.2.10, 10.50.2.30 (allowed hosts)

## Findings
72 connection records from 10.50.2.99 (source.mac 00-1B-21-AA-BB-99, no asset on record) to 24 addresses, 10.50.3.1 to 10.50.3.24, on ports 502, 102 and 44818, in under two minutes. 63 got no reply (state S0, addresses with no host), 6 were rejected (state REJ, live hosts with the port closed) and 3 completed (state SF): 10.50.3.11:502 (plc-line2-01), 10.50.3.12:102 (plc-line2-02) and 10.50.3.20:44818, an address with no asset on record. Zeek recorded no Modbus requests from this device. Not yet confirmed as malicious: it could be an unregistered asset-discovery tool.

## Incident handling (NIST SP 800-61 phases)
- Detect: Hunt, discovery hypothesis
- Analyse: Sweep pattern confirmed; owner of 10.50.2.99 and of 10.50.3.20 not yet known
- Contain: Pending: confirm the owner before blocking, in case it is an approved discovery tool
- Eradicate: n/a
- Recover: n/a

## NIS2 reporting (example of use, not a compliance claim)
Reportable? To be assessed
Clock started at: [UTC time the client became aware]
Early warning 24h: [to decide] | Notification 72h: [to decide] | Final report 1 month: [to decide]

## Handover
Next shift: find the switch port for MAC 00-1B-21-AA-BB-99, ask the client who owns 10.50.2.99 and 10.50.3.20, and check for any later traffic from the device.

description: Planned maintenance: TIA Portal on the engineering workstation opened three sessions to plc-line2-02. Accepted behaviour, exception proposed. Keywords: hunt, accepted-behaviour, ics, maintenance.
title: __RUN_DATE__ | CLIENT-B | Hunt: engineering software sessions to a controller (T0843, T0858) | Closed - Accepted Behaviour | TLP:GREEN

globalNotes.note:
TLP:GREEN | CLIENT-B

## Hypothesis
Engineering software sessions to a controller include unauthorised logic changes.

## Scope and data
Elastic Defend network events from the engineering workstation ot-eng-ws-01. Port 102 is S7 (Siemens). The endpoint sees the connection and byte counts, not the S7 requests inside it. Assets by IP (the sensor sees addresses, not names): ot-eng-ws-01 10.50.1.20, ot-hmi-01 10.50.2.10, ot-hist-01 10.50.2.30, plc-line2-01 10.50.3.11, plc-line2-02 10.50.3.12, ot-jump-01 10.50.0.5.

## Queries run
- process.name is Siemens.Automation.Portal.exe
- AND destination.port is 102

## Findings
Three network events: TIA Portal (Siemens.Automation.Portal.exe), user engineer1, opened three sessions to 10.50.3.12 (plc-line2-02) port 102, starting about ten minutes after the process started. The first lasted about 4 minutes 30 seconds and sent about 1.8 MB (received about 96 KB); the second 45 seconds (38 KB out, 22 KB in); the third 20 seconds (12 KB out, 9 KB in). A large first transfer then two short sessions looks like a program download followed by checks, but that is inferred from byte counts: the S7 requests are not visible here. The source, target and time match change record CHG-2041 (held outside this data). No other host or process connects to a controller on port 102 outside the allowlist in the same period. Accepted behaviour.

## Incident handling (NIST SP 800-61 phases)
- Detect: Hunt, intelligence-led
- Analyse: Source, target and timing match change record CHG-2041
- Contain: n/a
- Eradicate: n/a
- Recover: n/a

## NIS2 reporting (example of use, not a compliance claim)
Reportable? No
Clock started at: n/a
Early warning 24h: n/a | Notification 72h: n/a | Final report 1 month: n/a

## Handover
Add an exception for TIA Portal sessions from ot-eng-ws-01 to plc-line2-02, inside change windows only; keep the alert for any other process, host or controller. Revisit if the engineering workstation changes.

Report-ready summary: Three TIA Portal sessions from the engineering workstation to plc-line2-02 match change record CHG-2041; accepted behaviour, exception proposed (TLP:GREEN).

description: Two executables on a USB drive ran on the engineering workstation and one dropped a lookalike svchost32.exe. Confirmed and contained. Keywords: hunt, true-positive, ics, removable-media, t0847.
title: __RUN_DATE__ | CLIENT-B | Hunt: executables run from removable media on the engineering workstation (T0847) | Closed - True Positive | TLP:AMBER

eventNotes.note: autorun.exe run from E:\ProjectBackup, a USB device, unsigned. IOC: process.executable E:\ProjectBackup\autorun.exe.
update.exe (from the same USB drive) drops C:\Users\Public\svchost32.exe, a name imitating svchost.exe in a user-writable folder. IOC: file.path. Found by pivoting from update.exe.
The dropped svchost32.exe runs, unsigned, with update.exe as parent. Found by pivoting; not in the query results.

globalNotes.note:
TLP:AMBER | CLIENT-B

## Hypothesis
Malware is reaching the engineering workstation on removable media.

## Scope and data
Elastic Defend process and file events from ot-eng-ws-01 (user engineer1), with the device bus type added as a label (labels.bus_type) on processes launched from a USB device.

## Queries run
- labels.bus_type is usb (process launched from a USB device)

## Findings
Two events. explorer.exe started E:\ProjectBackup\autorun.exe, then autorun.exe started E:\ProjectBackup\update.exe, both unsigned and both from the USB drive. Pivoting on update.exe (outside the query results): it created C:\Users\Public\svchost32.exe, a name imitating svchost.exe in a user-writable folder, and started it, unsigned. svchost32.exe then started powershell.exe hidden (-nop -w hidden) to list C:\Projects, the engineering project folder. Treated as true positive.

## Incident handling (NIST SP 800-61 phases)
- Detect: Hunt, removable media hypothesis
- Analyse: USB-launched executables, dropped lookalike binary, hidden PowerShell listing project files
- Contain: Workstation isolated from the line 2 network after client approval; USB drive retrieved
- Eradicate: svchost32.exe, update.exe and autorun.exe removed; project files checked against a known-good backup
- Recover: Workstation reimaged; USB storage restricted by policy

## NIS2 reporting (example of use, not a compliance claim)
Reportable? Yes, to assess by the client against its thresholds
Clock started at: [UTC time the client became aware]
Early warning 24h: [done] | Notification 72h: [done] | Final report 1 month: [drafted]

## Handover
Closed. Client to trace where the USB drive came from and whether other engineering workstations saw it. Keep the removable-media process detection.

Keywords: hunt, true-positive, ics, removable-media, t0847
Report-ready summary: Two unsigned executables from a USB drive ran on the engineering workstation and dropped a lookalike svchost32.exe; true positive, contained (TLP:AMBER).

description: Negative-result hunt: all outbound traffic from the OT zone reviewed and explained as two scheduled, documented flows. No adversary activity found. Keywords: hunt, clean, negative-result, command-and-control.
title: __RUN_DATE__ | CLIENT-C | Hunt: C2 egress from the OT zone (T0885) | Closed - Clean, no adversary activity found | TLP:AMBER

globalNotes.note:
TLP:AMBER | CLIENT-C

## Hypothesis
A compromised OT host is calling out to infrastructure on the internet.

## Scope and data
DMZ firewall traffic logs (PAN-OS, observer ot-fw-dmz), last six hours, allowed outbound traffic to non-internal addresses. The only visibility is the firewall: no DNS, proxy or TLS inspection logs for the zone. Assets by IP (the sensor sees addresses, not names): ot-eng-ws-01 10.50.1.20, ot-hmi-01 10.50.2.10, ot-hist-01 10.50.2.30, plc-line2-01 10.50.3.11, plc-line2-02 10.50.3.12, ot-jump-01 10.50.0.5.

## Queries run
- network.direction is outbound
- AND destination.ip is not 10.0.0.0/8 (non-internal)

## Findings
18 events, from two hosts to two destinations, each matching a named firewall rule. 10.50.0.2 (ot-time-01) to 203.0.113.5 port 123 over UDP, application ntp, rule OT-DMZ-NTP-OUT, hourly, 6 events. 10.50.2.30 (ot-hist-01) to 198.51.100.20 port 443 over TCP, application ssl, rule OT-DMZ-HIST-REPL, every 30 minutes, 12 events of about 48 KB sent each. Both are periodic, but the intervals are the documented schedules (hourly time sync, half-hourly historian replication to the vendor cloud, per the client's firewall rule base). No other host leaves the zone, no unusual ports or volumes. No adversary activity found.

## Incident handling (NIST SP 800-61 phases)
- Detect: Hunt, intelligence-led
- Analyse: Two periodic flows reviewed against their firewall rules and documented schedules; coverage gaps listed
- Contain: n/a
- Eradicate: n/a
- Recover: n/a

## NIS2 reporting (example of use, not a compliance claim)
Reportable? No
Clock started at: n/a
Early warning 24h: n/a | Notification 72h: n/a | Final report 1 month: n/a

## Handover
Clean result for the stated scope. Re-run in 90 days or on new intelligence. Gap: no DNS, proxy or TLS inspection logs for the OT zone, so destination names and payloads are not visible and a beacon over an allowed destination would not show.

Keywords: hunt, clean, negative-result, command-and-control
Report-ready summary: Outbound traffic from the OT zone is two scheduled, documented flows; no adversary activity found, coverage gap noted (TLP:AMBER).
